Equipment copies connect the two layers. The first copy of an item contributes 1% of that item's base stats to the permanent collection total. Completing the copy progression raises the contribution to 3% in total. Accessories complete at three copies; other equipment families complete at twenty. The balance is &minus;3 AP: 30 &minus; 2: The balance is −3 AP: 30 − 28 + 3 − 8. The run reaches zero before every planned encounter occurs. The correct response is to change the plan: remove low-value fights, reach another boss earlier, or reduce the chance of a setback by upgrading first.
The balance is 12 AP: 30 &minus; 18 + 6: The balance is 12 AP: 30 − 18 + 6 − 6. Hard Mode turns one mistake into six ordinary victories of AP cost. A route that is comfortable in Normal Mode may therefore need stronger equipment, fewer optional encounters, or a larger reserve before the boss.
The balance is 15 AP: 30 &minus; 20 + 9: The balance is 15 AP: 30 − 20 + 9 − 4. A single defeat costs as much as four successful field battles. If those four battles were optional farming, avoiding the bad matchup would preserve the same AP while also protecting the run's momentum.
The balance is 22 AP: 30 − 14 + 6. The route creates progress and still leaves room for farming, a longer connection, or one failed fight. The useful lesson is not that 22 is always ideal; it is that the next choice can be made without immediate AP pressure.

The Normal Mode progression simulation r: The Normal Mode progression simulation runs 30 trials against the active boss, zone, enemy, item, and character assets. A simulated fresh player starts with the same 30 AP, base stats, six equipment slots, zero gold, and no collection. It buys affordable equipment, equips higher-value pieces, models duplicate drops and permanent collection bonuses, and chooses a farming zone only when its estimated chance of winning is at least 82%.
